newsitem.title: UK: British forces unhurt in Northern Irish incident.
newsitem.headline: British forces unhurt in Northern Irish incident.

text.p: British forces escaped injury in a suspected mortar attack by IRA guerrillas on a vehicle patrol in the Northern Ireland capital Belfast on Monday, security sources said.

Police said they were investigating an explosion in a stronghold of the pro-Irish Roman Catholic community in the west of the city as British armoured vehicles were on patrol. No one was hurt and security vehicles were not hit.
Security has been tightened across Northern Ireland after an upsurge in IRA (Irish Republican Army) activity which provoked two retaliatory attacks by pro-British Loyalist extremists.
The IRA, fighting to unite the province with the Irish republic, abandoned a 17-month truce in February last year and set off a string of bombs in London.
It extended the campaign to Northern Ireland last October, killing a soldier in a double carbomb attack at British Army headquarters at Lisburn, 10 miles (15 km) south of Belfast.
Britain says the IRA must declare a new ceasefire before its political wing Sinn Fein can secure a seat in the current multi-party talks on the divided province's future.
